root_cause: The OpenVINO Tokenizers build uses CMake FetchContent to download the sentencepiece v0.2.1 release tarball directly from github.com/google/sentencepiece/releases. The ARM64 merge-queue runner's outbound HTTPS request to that release-asset URL received an HTTP 500 Internal Server Error from GitHub's edge (x-github-edge-region: westus2), a transient upstream/CDN availability issue unrelated to the PR's actual change (constant offset alignment in .bin serialization, scoped to src/core/src/xml_util/ and its tests). This is the same failure mode recorded for the identical URL three hours earlier in run 36863877140 (HTTP 504), confirming github.com release-asset fetches for this specific job are an ongoing soft spot rather than a one-off.
reproduction_steps: Not reliably reproducible locally since it depends on a transient GitHub release-asset CDN hiccup. To attempt: on an aarch64 Linux host, run `pip wheel ./src/bindings/python/tools/openvino_tokenizers` (or trigger the 'OpenVINO tokenizers extension' CI job) and observe the CMake FetchContent_Populate step fetching https://github.com/google/sentencepiece/releases/download/v0.2.1/sentencepiece-0.2.1.tar.gz; a transient 5xx from GitHub during that window reproduces the failure.
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed 'OpenVINO tokenizers extension' job; no code change needed (attempt 2 was already in progress at investigation time).

Mirror the sentencepiece release tarball (and other FetchContent-based third-party sources such as pcre2) through an internal artifact cache/proxy to remove the hard dependency on github.com release-asset CDN availability during merge-queue builds.

Add retry/backoff around the CMake FetchContent download step for third-party sources fetched directly from github.com releases (e.g., a pre-fetch script with curl --retry, or CMake's URL download retry options).
prevention_strategies: Mirror or cache third-party FetchContent sources (sentencepiece, pcre2, etc.) in an internally controlled location, and/or wrap FetchContent downloads with automatic retry logic to absorb transient GitHub release-asset 5xx responses without failing the whole merge-queue run.
historical_context: This is the second occurrence of the exact same sentencepiece-0.2.1.tar.gz download failure in roughly 3 hours: run 36863877140 (PR #38536, 2026-10-01T13:27:03Z) hit HTTP 504 on the identical URL; this run hit HTTP 500. An earlier, related but distinct pattern (2baab38e090720ec) recorded a pcre2-10.48.zip download failure for the same job on 2026-09-21 (HTTP 504, PR #38190). All three point to the same root cause: this job's direct dependency on github.com release-asset CDN availability during the FetchContent step.
